correctness.summary: Leaf nodes emit ALL contained point indices when the node's region merely OVERLAPS the query box, never testing individual point coordinates. This returns false positives — indices of points that lie outside the query rectangle.
correctness.triggeringInput: Build with xs/ys/zs = {(0,0,0),(10,0,0)}, n=2, maxDepth large enough that these two points share a leaf only if they cannot be separated; simplest: points (0,0,0) and (9,9,9) with maxDepth=0 so the single root is a leaf containing both. Then RangeQuery with box x1=y1=z1=-1, x2=y2=z2=1 (contains only the first point). The root region overlaps the box (passes line 56), the root is a leaf (all C<0), so it emits BOTH index 0 and index 1, even though point (9,9,9) is outside the query box. Returns count=2 with a wrong index.
correctness.rootCause: In the leaf branch (line 57) the code does `for (int i = 0; i < n->Count; i++) outIdx[i] = n->FirstIndex + i;` emitting every point in the leaf unconditionally. The node-region test on line 56 only rejects nodes whose bounding region is DISJOINT from the query box; a partially-overlapping leaf still contains points outside the box. Unlike RangeTree.QueryRec / SegmentTree which test each point, Octree never filters individual points against (x1,y1,z1)-(x2,y2,z2).
correctness.suggestedFix: In the leaf branch, test each point against the query box before emitting: for each i in [0,Count), let g = FirstIndex+i and only append g if xs[g]>=x1 && xs[g]<=x2 && ys[g]>=y1 && ys[g]<=y2 && zs[g]>=z1 && zs[g]<=z2. This requires RangeQuery to also receive xs/ys/zs pointers (currently it does not), so the signature must be extended to pass the coordinate arrays for per-point filtering.

perf.summary: Octant index computed twice per point (count pass + scatter pass); cache it in a stackalloc byte buffer and reuse.
perf.currentCost: GetOctIdx is called once in the counting loop (line 33) and again in the scatter loop (line 35) for every point in [start,end). That is 2 calls x (3 compares + 3 ORs) per point per recursion level, i.e. O(n) redundant index recomputation at every tree level (O(n log n) total wasted GetOctIdx evaluations and 2x redundant loads of xs/ys/zs).
perf.proposedChange: Allocate `byte* oct = stackalloc byte[n];` alongside tx/ty/tz. In the first loop store `byte o = (byte)GetOctIdx(...); oct[i-start]=o; counts[o]++;`. In the scatter loop read `int idx = oct[i-start];` instead of recomputing. This also removes the second set of xs[i]/ys[i]/zs[i] loads needed only for the index.
perf.rationale: Halves the GetOctIdx work and eliminates one full re-read of the three coordinate streams per node, trading 6 FP compares/point for one byte load/store. Fewer cycles and fewer dependent loads in the hottest build loop; byte buffer is tiny and stays in L1.
perf.risk: None to semantics — identical partition. Adds n bytes of stack per recursion frame; n shrinks down the tree so peak extra stack is bounded by root n. Keep `byte` (0..7 fits).

perf.summary: stackalloc of tx/ty/tz uses the full [start,end) span at every recursion level, compounding stack usage along the deepest path.
perf.currentCost: Each BuildRec frame that partitions allocates 3*n doubles (24*n bytes) of scratch where n=end-start. Along a recursion path the live frames stack their scratch; worst case the sum over the path can approach 24*N*maxDepth bytes of stack in pathological splits, risking stack overflow for large N on mobile (small thread stacks).
perf.proposedChange: Allocate the tx/ty/tz scratch once in Build() sized to the root n (or accept a caller-provided scratch pointer per the Try*/Run convention) and pass it down, reusing the same buffer at each level since partition is done before recursing into children.
perf.rationale: Caller-provided or once-allocated scratch caps scratch RAM at 24*N bytes total instead of growing per recursion frame, removing a mobile stack-overflow hazard and reducing stack-probe/touch cost.
perf.risk: Scratch is consumed before BuildChildren recurses, so a single shared buffer is safe (no overlap between a parent's partition and its children's). Must size to root n. Changes Build signature if exposed as a scratch param (ergonomics tradeoff).

perf.summary: Recomputes mx,my,mz which were already computed (as x+size/2 etc.) by the caller for PartitionOctants.
perf.currentCost: PartitionOctants is called with x+size/2, y+size/2, z+size/2 (line 25), then BuildChildren recomputes mx=x+half, my=y+half, mz=z+half (line 41) where half==size/2. Two extra adds (size/2 already equals half). Minor but per-node.
perf.proposedChange: Compute `double half = size/2, mx = x+half, my = y+half, mz = z+half;` once in BuildRec and pass mx/my/mz into both PartitionOctants and BuildChildren, dropping the recompute and the inner `x + size/2` expressions.
perf.rationale: Removes 3 redundant adds and a divide-vs-half mismatch per internal node; tightens the per-node dependency chain.
perf.risk: size/2 and half are bit-identical (same double divide), so midpoints are identical — fully semantics-preserving.

perf.summary: Leaf detection does 8 child-pointer compares even though the build already stores Count; recursion also re-checks each child >=0 after the all-negative test.
perf.currentCost: Every visited node runs an 8-way `Ci<0` AND chain (line 57) to detect a leaf, then on internal nodes re-tests each `Ci>=0` (lines 59-66). A leaf node here is exactly one with end-start<=1 or depth>=maxDepth; the node already carries Count and could carry an explicit leaf flag, avoiding the 8-compare scan on the hot query path.
perf.proposedChange: Mark leaves at build time (e.g. set C0=-2 sentinel or a dedicated IsLeaf via reusing sign of Count) and test a single condition for the leaf fast-path; for internal nodes the per-child `>=0` guard is still needed but the leaf scan is removed.
perf.rationale: Replaces an 8-term boolean reduction at every node with one branch on the common leaf path, shortening the query's per-node critical path in a recursive hot loop.
perf.risk: Must pick a sentinel that cannot collide with valid node indices (>=0). Adds one store at build time. Behavior identical if the leaf predicate matches the original all-children-negative condition exactly.
